text:
jamie.ops: incident-bot: Pager: canary cohort B error-rate jumped to 11.8% after deploy r2026-05-10. Auto-suppress not triggered. Paging oncall @miguel.sre

miguel.sre: on it — pulling logs and tracing now. Can anyone confirm which commit landed to cohort B?

deploy-bot: Release r2026-05-10 deployed to canary-B (region: us-west-2). Commit: abc1234f. Healthchecks passed initially.

sana.eng: I see increased 500s from the tokenizer service right after abc1234f — looks like a header-parsing edge-case. Spike aligns with 10:42:11 UTC.

jamie.ops: Risk assessment: user-facing latency for conversational endpoints up ~40% for affected cohort. Customer-facing sessions erroring intermittently. Recommend immediate mitigation: revert commit abc1234f from canary and hold rollout.

miguel.sre: agree. rolling a quick single-commit revert on canary-B now. Command I'm running:
```bash
# revert to previous commit on release branch
git revert --no-edit abc1234f && git push origin release/r2026-05-10 && deployctl rollout canary-B --revision=head
```

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline started for revert (r2026-05-10-revert-abc1234f). Canary-B rollout initiated.

carol.cs: Heads-up to support: customers in cohort-B may see intermittent failures for up to ~15 minutes. I'm drafting a short blurb for the in-app status and support playbook.

sana.eng: logs show request examples that triggered the bug: missing X-Client-Locale header -> tokenizer blew up. Adding a guard would be quick but revert is lower risk.

miguel.sre: Revert finished on canary-B. Observability: error-rate back down to baseline within 2m. CPU and tail latency normalizing.

deploy-bot: Canary-B status: healthy. Rollback succeeded. No further action taken on global rollout (paused).

jamie.ops: Good. Next steps: 1) keep rollout paused, 2) prepare a tiny hotfix that adds a header guard + unit test, 3) run small canary against additional synthetic load. Who owns hotfix?

sana.eng: I can pick up the hotfix branch now, will target a single-line guard and test. Plan: patch -> CI -> canary-A then canary-B. ETA ~20–30m.

carol.cs: Support blurb posted to status page and my triage doc. Notifying top 3 customers that hit the error.

miguel.sre: handing back to oncall rotation — keeping an eye on monitoring for 30m. If spike returns, we'll escalate to full rollback and notify infra.

jamie.ops: Thanks all. Filed short incident note in #postmortems (will expand after hotfix). Assigning follow-up: release-manager to coordinate the canary plan and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
